documents.title: Assumption of Our Lady Parish Church
documents.content:
Assumption of Our Lady Parish Church

One of the oldest churches in Leyte, founded in 1704 (the town's Historic Church era). Built by Jesuit missionaries with coral stone walls, it was originally constructed as a fortress against Moro raids and later the 1897 tidal wave.

Features
Baroque architecture with an ornate baroque facade
Houses the image of Nuestra Señora de la Asuncion, one of the oldest Marian images in the province
Home to precious relics chronicling Tanauan's spiritual journey
Under restoration as a national cultural treasure under the National Historical Commission

The town celebrates its fiesta every August 15 — see Religion in Tanauan and Pasaka Festival.

See also: History of Tanauan, Culture and Heritage of Tanauan.

documents.title: Barangays of Tanauan
documents.content:
Barangays of Tanauan

Tanauan, Leyte is divided into 54 barangays. A Barangay Registry Directory at the /Barangays page lets visitors search each barangay's history, leadership, contact details, gallery, and portals.

Named barangays (seed registry)
Ada, Amanluran, Arado, Atipolo, Balud, Bangon, Bantagan, Baras, Binolo, Binongtoan, Bislig, Cabalagnan, Cabonga-an, Cabuynan, Cahumayhumayan, Calogcog, Calsadahay, Camire, Canbalisara, Canramos, Catigbian, Catmon, Cogon, Guindag-an, Guingauan, Hilagpad, Kiling, Lapay, Licod, Linao, Magay, Maghulod, Malaguicay, Maribi, Mohon, Pago, Pasil, Picas, Sacme, Salvador, Solano, Talolora, Tugop.

Many barangays have rich folklore origin stories (e.g. Barangay Arado named after the plough "arado," Atipolo after the fruit-bearing Atipolo tree, Camire/Canramos for its potters). See Culture and Heritage of Tanauan for the town's broader heritage.

> Note: contact/leadership details shown on the seed registry are placeholders to be maintained by the LGU. For the authoritative list and current officials, use the live registry at /Barangays and the Offices directory.

See also: Geography of Tanauan, Demographics of Tanauan, Municipal Government of Tanauan.

documents.title: Climate of Tanauan
documents.content:
Climate of Tanauan

Tanauan features a tropical climate (Type II) in the Philippine climate classification, with no pronounced dry season and abundant rainfall mostly from November to January.
Average temperature: ~27.5°C (range 24–32°C through the year, high humidity)
Annual rainfall: ~2,337 mm
Average humidity: ~85%

Located along the eastern seaboard, the municipality is prone to monsoons and typhoons. This climate supports year-round farming and fishing. Residents are advised to stay alert during typhoon season and plan agricultural activities accordingly.

See also: Geography of Tanauan, Demographics of Tanauan.

documents.title: Culture and Heritage of Tanauan
documents.content:
Culture and Heritage of Tanauan

Tanauan, Leyte has 316+ years of history, 5 heritage sites, 3 traditional dances, and 1 annual festival.

Heritage sites (as featured on the website)

1. Assumption of Our Lady Parish Church (est. 1704) — Jesuit-built coral stone church, baroque facade, home to Nuestra Señora de la Asuncion.
2. Balinsasayaw Singers — a celebrated choral ensemble named after the balinsasayaw (swiftlet bird), preserving traditional Waray folk music; recorded folk songs like "Singsing" and performed at cultural events across the Philippines.
3. Pasaka Festival — a vibrant thanksgiving festival every August in honor of Tanauan's patroness, Our Lady of the Assumption.
4. Tanauan Public Plaza — gathering place beneath centuries-old acacia trees, with a mini-amphitheater hosting cultural performances and civic events.
5. Tanauan Municipal Hall (est. 1910) — seat of local governance, blending traditional Filipino municipal design with modern infrastructure.
6. Tanauan Airstrip — a historical World War II site built by American forces.
7. Surge of Hope — a community resilience project symbolizing unity and shared responsibility.
8. Hanging Bride (Brgy Balud tradition) — a rare cultural ritual and folklore tradition preserving ancestral practices in Barangay Balud.

Related cultural identity
Pottery & crafts: Barangay Canramos is renowned for its potters and quality clay.
Balinsasayaw Singers continue to entertain local and international visitors, with Danny Basas as musical director and composer of the Tanauan Hymn.
Skimboarding is a popular coastal water sport — see Skimboarding in Tanauan.

See also: History of Tanauan, Pasaka Festival, Traditional Products of Tanauan.

documents.title: Demographics of Tanauan
documents.content:
Demographics of Tanauan

Population
2020 Census of Population and Housing (1 May 2020): population of 57,455 across 54 barangays, within a land area of ~78.4 km².
2024 official census (1 July 2024): growth to about 60,212 residents, a modest increase over four years.
2015 Census: 13,518 households with an average size of about 4.1 persons.
Source: PSA Eastern Visayas Special Release (May–July 2025).

> Note: The Sanitation/RHU data cites a population of 62,533 and 16,644 households (Q2 2025). Figures vary by source and date.

Language & religion

Most residents speak Waray-Waray, with Filipino and English widely understood (see Languages of Tanauan). The population is predominantly Roman Catholic, with Iglesia ni Cristo, Evangelicals, and Protestants present (see Religion in Tanauan).

Livelihood

Major income sources include agriculture, fishing, and micro-enterprises.

See also: Geography of Tanauan, Languages of Tanauan, Religion in Tanauan, Barangays of Tanauan.

documents.title: Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO)
documents.content:
Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO)

The Municipal Agriculture Office supports Tanauan's farmers, fisherfolk, and backyard raisers with free seeds, fertilizer grants, motorized banca supplies, and fair market prices. Located at the Ground Floor, Right Wing, Municipal Hall. Agri hotline: (053) 322-5401.

Crop section
RSBSA registration (Corn & Cassava) — Registry System for Basic Sectors in Agriculture; reliable data for program implementation and policy.
Rice section — seed & fertilizer distribution, crop insurance claims, RSBSA registration of rice farmers, geotagged confirmation of rice areas.
Vegetables — subsidizes high-value-crop farmers to increase production.
Farm machinery/equipment — mechanization of farmlands, helping defray rental fees and boosting yield.

Livestock section
Medicines & vaccines to prevent deadly diseases of cattle and domesticated animals
Livestock dispersal for eligible farmers to improve income and livelihood

Fisheries section
RSBSA/NFRS registration and boat registration (master list of fisherfolk)
Fingerlings dispersal for income and livelihood

Institutional development
Assistance registering farmers'/fisherfolk associations
Livelihood assistance to address poverty

Each barangay has an assigned agricultural technologist for on-farm assistance. The office also runs a Tanauan Indicative Price Watch for fair market buying prices.

See also: Departments of Tanauan, Municipal Government of Tanauan.

documents.title: Municipal Civil Registrar
documents.content:
Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR)

The Office of the Municipal Civil Registrar of Tanauan, Leyte implements civil registration programs pursuant to the Civil Registry Law (Act No. 3753).
Location: Ground Floor, Tanauan Town Hall, Real Street, Tanauan, Leyte
Department Head: Vincent Francis A. Salvaña
Staff / Personnel: Virginia Parmo, Miracelo Vertudes, Ma. Clenia Pilola
Citizen's Charter Route: /citizens-charter/civil-registrar

Services Offered

1. Application for Documents (Birth, Marriage, Death Certificates)
About: Registration and issuance of certified copies of birth, marriage, and death events within the prescribed period.
Processing Time: Approximately 34 minutes
Fee: ₱80.00
Requirements:
Birth: Marriage Contract of Parents, PSA Negative Certificate of the Child, Baptismal Certificate, Affidavit of 2 Disinterested Persons (for delayed registration), Current CTC / Valid ID, Affidavit to Use the Surname of the Father (AUSF, if parents are unmarried).
Marriage: Copy of Certificate of Marriage (COM) for registration; for delayed registration: joint affidavit of applicants duly notarized, PSA negative result, old copy of unregistered document.
Death: Personal appearance of informant (spouse or nearest kin) if death occurred at home; Death Certificate prepared by hospital if death occurred in hospital.
Procedure:
  1. Proceed to the MCR and verbalize request.
  2. If document is available, proceed to the Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) for payment.
  3. Present Official Receipt (OR) to registry clerk.
  4. Certificate is checked, signed, and issued.

2. Application for Marriage License
About: Filing sworn applications for marriage license before contracting marriage.
Processing Time: 10 days and 1 hour (subject to mandatory 10-day legal posting period).
Fee: ₱150.00
Requirements:
Pre-marital Counselling Certificate
Birth or Baptismal Certificate of contracting parties, Valid ID, CTC
Parental Consent (if aged 18–20)
Parental Advice (if aged 21–24)
Certificate of No Marriage (CENOMAR) from PSA
Duly notarized Affidavit of Cohabitation (for couples cohabiting for 5+ years)

MSWDO — Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office

Mandate

Office hours

Requirements: Letter of Intent / proposal, valid ID photocopy.

documents.title: Geography of Tanauan
documents.content:
Geography of Tanauan

Location

Tanauan is located in the eastern part of Leyte, facing the Leyte Gulf. It is bordered by Palo to the north and Tolosa to the south. It is approximately 18 kilometers south of Tacloban City and accessible via the Maharlika Highway.

Land area & terrain
Total land area: 78.63 km² (the Demographics page cites ~78.4 km²)
Terrain: mostly flat, with some rolling hills in the western part; both coastal and inland zones

Administrative divisions

Tanauan is divided into 54 barangays — see Barangays of Tanauan.

Climate

Tanauan has a tropical climate (Type II) with no pronounced dry season and abundant rainfall mostly from November to January. Temperatures range 24–32°C with high humidity; it is prone to monsoons and typhoons. See Climate of Tanauan.

See also: History of Tanauan, Demographics of Tanauan, Climate of Tanauan.

documents.title: History of Tanauan
documents.content:
History of Tanauan

Tanauan, Leyte was established in 1701 and has over 300 years of recorded history. It is known as the "Cradle of Intellectuals" (Bungto Han Kamag-araman) for producing many remarkable figures in Philippine history since the Spanish colonial period.

The name "Tanauan"

The name comes from "tan-awan" (pronounced /tan-a-wan/), a lookout tower. The town derived its name from a majestic Molave tree that served as a natural lookout for early inhabitants. A sentinel watched from the tree for Moro pirates raiding coastal communities, and a hollow trunk called a bayog was hung from the tree and struck to signal danger, prompting residents to take refuge in a stone-walled fort called a cuta.

Founding families

The first settlers were the family of Calanao (father) and Makasanay (mother) and their daughter Sangad, living by the banks of the Bukid River at the base of Adil Hill. In 1661, Juanillo Siengco, a Chinese mestizo from Sugbo (Cebu), with his wife Susana Baga and companions Cornelio and Elias, journeyed to the eastern coast of Leyte along the Binahaan River and discovered fertile lands.

The two groups forged a pact of friendship and lived in harmony. In time, Juanillo's son Josef married Calanao's daughter Sangad; their five daughters and one son — Anurya, Alimocon, Atalabong, Dolido, and Tombalasay — formed the tribe that laid the groundwork for Tanauan's first town officials.

World War II and Liberation

Following General Douglas MacArthur's landing on Red Beach in Palo on October 20, 1944, Tanauan became a crucial strategic site. The US Sixth Army established its headquarters here and a vital airfield (the Tanauan Airstrip) was constructed. Mayor Pedro A. Villegas and his secretary Janario Perez refused to serve Japanese forces and joined the guerrilla resistance. The 312th Bombardment Group also operated in the area.

Resilience through disasters

From the tidal wave of 1897 that the historic church withstood, to Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) in November 2013, Tanauan has repeatedly demonstrated its capacity for recovery and rebuilding. The town motto: "The spirit of the Tanauananon cannot be broken—only strengthened."

See also: Assumption of Our Lady Parish Church, Pasaka Festival, Geography of Tanauan, Tanauan Airstrip.

documents.title: Languages of Tanauan
documents.content:
Languages of Tanauan

Primary language: Waray-Waray

Waray-Waray (specifically the Leyte-Waray dialect variant) is the primary native language spoken by nearly the entire population of Tanauan. It is the bedrock of everyday social interaction, trade, folk culture, and family life, and is widely spoken at home, in schools, and in community-level administration.

Bilingual/multilingual literacy (estimates)
Waray-Waray (native): ~98.5%
Filipino / Tagalog (bilingual): ~92.0%
English (business & education): ~85.5%

Education: MTB-MLE

Tanauan's elementary schools implement the Mother Tongue-Based Multilingual Education (MTB-MLE) framework under the Philippine Department of Education. From Kindergarten to Grade 3, Waray-Waray is the primary medium of instruction, gradually transitioning to Filipino and English.

Governance & media

Local announcements, public health campaigns, and community forums are typically conducted in Waray-Waray across all 54 barangays. Official municipal documentation, legal ordinances, and business licenses are formulated in English, with Filipino often used in ceremonial events.

See also: Demographics of Tanauan, Culture and Heritage of Tanauan.

documents.title: Mayor's Office
documents.content:
Mayor's Office

The Mayor's Office is the chief executive office of the Municipality of Tanauan, Leyte. The current Municipal Mayor is Hon. Ma. Gina E. Merilo.

Role
The Mayor leads the executive branch of the municipal government, directing municipal departments, implementing ordinances and national law, and guiding municipal development. See Municipal Government of Tanauan and Vision and Mission of Tanauan for the municipality's strategic direction.

Visit
Mayor's Corner (/Mayors Corner) — leadership messages, policy directions, and guidance on municipal development.
Municipal Officials (/Municipal-Officials) — the full slate of current officials.

See also: Municipal Government of Tanauan, Vision and Mission of Tanauan.

documents.title: Municipal Government of Tanauan
documents.content:
Municipal Government of Tanauan

Tanauan, Leyte is governed by a municipal government under the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), headed by the elected Mayor and Vice Mayor, with the Sangguniang Bayan as the legislative body and 30+ municipal departments/offices as the executive arm. The municipality comprises 54 barangays (see Barangays of Tanauan).

Structure
Mayor's Office — the chief executive, currently Hon. Ma. Gina E. Merilo.
Vice Mayor & Sangguniang Bayan — presides over the council; 10 SB Members (1st–8th councilors, ABC President, SK Fed. President).
Departments directory: see Departments of Tanauan.

Key public-facing services
Business permits & licensing (Business Permit and Licensing Section)
Taxes & fees (Taxes and Fees of Tanauan, Municipal Treasurer's Office)
Social welfare (MSWDO), health (MHO/RHU), sanitation, civil registry, and more.

Transparency
The municipality publishes bids and awards, a full disclosure portal, and annual accomplishment reports per office (see Taxes and Fees of Tanauan and department pages).

See also: Vision and Mission of Tanauan, Departments of Tanauan, Mayor's Office.

documents.title: Pasaka Festival
documents.content:
Pasaka Festival

The Pasaka Festival is Tanauan's signature annual celebration. The name is derived from the Waray word meaning "to invite," and honors the Assumption of Our Lady while commemorating Tanauan's cultural heritage. (Some heritage copy describes "Pasaka" as a term inviting progress, health, and good fortune.) It began in 1969 as a humble thanksgiving ritual and has grown into one of Eastern Visayas' most spectacular cultural events.

When & where
Every August 1–15 in Tanauan, Leyte (peak near the town fiesta on Aug 15).
55+ years of tradition.

Festival highlights
Street dancing — colorful costumes, synchronized choreography, rhythmic drumbeats
Religious procession — solemn procession of the Señor Santo Niño
Community feast — local delicacies and traditional Waray cuisine
Float parade — floats representing different barangays telling stories of faith and heritage
Cultural exhibits — Waray art, craftsmanship, historical artifacts
Live entertainment — concerts, talent shows, local and national artists

Timeline
1969: beginnings honoring the Señor Santo Niño and the town's foundation anniversary
1980s: regional recognition; more barangays joined with floats and synchronized dances
1990s: street-dancing competitions formalized; performers from neighboring municipalities
2013: after Typhoon Yolanda, Pasaka became a symbol of hope and resilience
Today: one of the Philippines' most vibrant cultural celebrations

Records
Grand Champion honors at the Aliwan Fiesta and Pintados-Kasadyaan. Recent festival archives show themes such as "Unity in Faith" (2024), "Rising Together" (2023), "Hope Renewed" (2022).

See also: Culture and Heritage of Tanauan, Assumption of Our Lady Parish Church, Religion in Tanauan.

documents.title: Religion in Tanauan
documents.content:
Religion in Tanauan

Tanauan is predominantly Roman Catholic. Its spiritual life is centered on the Assumption of Our Lady Parish Church, one of the oldest in Leyte, founded in the early 18th century. The church has survived natural disasters and wars through centuries of devotion.

Annual fiesta

The town celebrates its annual fiesta every August 15, the Feast of the Assumption, with religious processions, novenas, and community events (overlapping with the Pasaka Festival). In 2025, the parish celebrated its 315th year anniversary with food drives, inter-barangay masses, and youth catechism workshops.

Other religious communities include Iglesia ni Cristo, Evangelicals, and Protestants.

See also: Assumption of Our Lady Parish Church, History of Tanauan, Demographics of Tanauan.

documents.title: Skimboarding in Tanauan
documents.content:
Skimboarding in Tanauan

Tanauan, Leyte is becoming one of the Philippines' most exciting skimboarding destinations. Located on the eastern coast of Leyte facing the Leyte Gulf, its beaches offer a strong coastal culture ideal for the sport.

What is skimboarding?

Skimboarding is a variation of surfing that doesn't depend on big waves. Riders "skim" the surface on the shore break — riding when the wave crashes and recedes to sea. It combines elements of surfing and skateboarding, requiring speed, balance, and agility. The National Skimboarding event was organized "right where it started" in Tanauan.

Key spot
Santo Niño Beach — the heart of Tanauan skimboarding (with other beaches offering conditions for different skill levels)

Practical info
Best during summer months when waves are ideal
Tanauan has produced skilled skimboarders who compete in local and regional events
Plan your visit from Manila (flight to Tacloban, ~18 km away) or Cebu

See also: Geography of Tanauan, Tourism in Tanauan, Culture and Heritage of Tanauan.

documents.title: Tanauan Airstrip
documents.content:
Tanauan Airstrip

A historical World War II site built by American forces, the Tanauan Airstrip played a crucial role in the liberation of Leyte and the Pacific campaign. Following MacArthur's October 1944 landing, the US Sixth Army set up headquarters in Tanauan and constructed a vital airfield.

Though little remains today, the site stands as a testament to Tanauan's strategic importance in Philippine history during the Allied liberation campaign.

See also: History of Tanauan, Culture and Heritage of Tanauan.

documents.title: Taxes and Fees of Tanauan
documents.content:
Taxes and Fees of Tanauan

Real Property Tax (RPT)
Imposed on owners of land, buildings, and machinery within Tanauan.
Standard rate: 1% of the property's assessed value annually
Basic deadline: March 31 for full annual payment
Early payments qualify for up to 10% discount
Late payments incur penalties (see the on-page estimator)

Business Taxes & Licenses
Levied on registered businesses operating in the municipality, computed on gross sales or receipts from the preceding calendar year.
Filing period: January 1–20 annually
Requires an updated community tax certificate (Cedula)
Regulatory permits (Fire, Sanitary, Zoning) are bundled during assessment
Business tax gross rate ~1.5% of annual gross receipts (per estimator)

Regulatory & Administrative Fees
Miscellaneous public charges for clearances, health certs, civil registries, and public services:
Zoning clearances & building inspection permits
Municipal health card certificates
Civil registry (birth, marriage, death certificate processing)

Payment steps (Municipal Hall)
1. Assessment — present tax declarations (RPT) or gross revenue receipts (business) at the Assessor's Office
2. Verification — the Municipal Treasurer evaluates the computation, verifying penalties and discounts
3. Payment & O.R. — settle via Cashier or accredited banking systems; receive your Official Receipt immediately

Estimates derive from the Local Revenue Code of Tanauan and exclude administrative clearances and specific fire-department evaluation charges.

See also: Municipal Assessor's Office, Municipal Treasurer's Office, Business Permit & Licensing.

documents.title: Tourism in Tanauan
documents.content:
Tourism in Tanauan

Tanauan, Leyte is a coastal municipality facing the Leyte Gulf that has grown into a tourism and cultural destination. Key attractions and experiences:
Pasaka Festival — the town's signature thanksgiving festival, every August 1–15
Assumption of Our Lady Parish Church — a 1704 Jesuit-built coral stone church
Culture and Heritage of Tanauan — heritage sites, the Balinsasayaw Singers, and traditional dances
Traditional Products of Tanauan — Binagol, moron, clay pottery, and sun-dried harvests
Skimboarding in Tanauan — a top Philippine skimboarding destination (Santo Niño Beach)
Tanauan Airstrip — a World War II history site

Toward its 2032 Vision and Mission of Tanauan, the municipality aims to be a "premier tourism destination, education hub, and investment haven" in Leyte.

See also: Geography of Tanauan, Culture and Heritage of Tanauan.

documents.title: Traditional Products of Tanauan
documents.content:
Traditional Products of Tanauan

Tanauan's local goods span sweet delicacies and handcrafted treasures — "from riverbed clay pottery to sun-dried ocean harvests."

Signature delicacies

Binagol (the legendary pasalubong)
Tanauan's 1 pasalubong and the "sweet soul of Eastern Visayas." Made from mountain talyan taro, slow-simmered coconut milk, and muscovado caramel. Served in an authentic halved coconut shell (bagol) and wrapped in banana leaves, with a smooth, velvety taro crust over a pool of golden coconut caramel. Best enjoyed warm with hot sikwate (cacao). An ancestral Visayan recipe.

Moron
A silky swirl of chocolate moron — a native staple, typically enjoyed with sikwate.

Sigarilyas / other crafts
Binagol, moron, and other coconut- & taro-based sweets
Riverbed clay pottery (Barangay Canramos is renowned for potters; see Culture and Heritage of Tanauan)
Sun-dried ocean harvests (local fishing products)

Products are 100% locally grown and harvested, with generations of traditional craftsmanship.

See also: Culture and Heritage of Tanauan, Tourism in Tanauan.

documents.title: Vision and Mission of Tanauan
documents.content:
Vision and Mission of Tanauan

Vision

> "Tanauan by 2032, a 1st class municipality which is a premier tourism destination, education hub, and an investment haven in the province of Leyte — inhabited by a healthy and empowered citizenry living in peaceful and resilient communities; with a competitive, diversified, dynamic, and inclusive economy; a disaster-proof, quality, and adequate social support and infrastructure system; and an ecologically balanced, sustainable, and aesthetic environment — under an effective and efficient participatory and people-centered leadership with a strong political will."

Mission

> "The Municipal Government of Tanauan shall take the lead in the integration and implementation of programs, projects, and activities; promote strong multi-sectoral level partnerships; and mobilize resources through a strong political will and unity of purpose."

Core values
Integrity — honest & transparent governance
Excellence — striving for the highest standards
Accountability — responsible public service
Teamwork — collaborative partnerships
Service — people-centered approach
Resilience — disaster-ready communities

Quality policy

Competent leadership, continuous improvement, citizen satisfaction, and sustainable development.

See also: Mayor's Office, Municipal Government of Tanauan.
